h1: Earned settlement earnings thresholds: the 3, 5, 10 and 20-year routes explained
intro: On 2 November 2026 the Home Office confirmed its earned settlement plans, where how soon you can get ILR depends largely on what you earn. Here we set out the earned settlement earnings thresholds for each route, the other conditions, and what we know about when the new rules will start.

sections.heading: Earned settlement earnings thresholds at a glance
sections.text:
- 3 years: earnings of £125,141 in three of the last four years, or membership of a highest talent group still to be defined.
- 5 years: earnings of £50,271 in three of the last five years, five years in an eligible public service job such as doctor, nurse or teacher, or a British connection.
- 10 years: the new standard route, with earnings of at least £12,571 in five of the previous seven years. Couples can combine earnings to reach £25,142.
- 20 years: for people whose immigration breaches or use of public funds stop them qualifying sooner.

The earlier proposal for a 15-year route for jobs below degree level has been dropped.

sections.heading: Conditions for every route
sections.text:
As well as meeting the earnings test, applicants will need to:
- speak English to a high standard
- have no criminal record
- have no outstanding debts to the government
- have paid National Insurance for at least three years

The 3, 5 and 10-year routes aren’t open to people who have claimed public funds in the last five years or have a qualifying immigration breach.

sections.heading: Who keeps a 5-year route
sections.text:
Some groups who were already on their route before the May 2025 White Paper keep a five-year path:
- care workers who met their visa conditions, including earning at least £25,000 a year in the sector
- some health and education workers in jobs below degree level who arrived before May 2025
- Hong Kong BN(O) visa holders, armed forces members and some legacy routes

Others already in the UK will generally move onto the new framework, on the 10-year route unless they qualify for a faster one.

sections.heading: When do the earned settlement rules start?
sections.text:
They haven’t started yet. The government says changes will begin to be laid in the December 2026 Immigration Rules and will be brought in over the course of 2027, with detailed guidance to follow. Until the new rules apply to you, the current settlement rules continue.

Separately, the English level for settlement rises to B2 from 26 March 2027. Read our news story on [B2 English for ILR](/blog/b2-english-for-ilr/).

sections.heading: How earned settlement earnings are likely to be counted
sections.text: The thresholds refer to earnings over several years, so keep good records: payslips, P60s, tax returns and bank statements. If your income comes from self-employment, a company you own or several jobs, the evidence rules will matter, and these haven’t been published yet. Couples should keep evidence of both incomes.

sections.heading: How we can help
sections.text: We can work out which route you’re likely to qualify for, when, and what evidence to start keeping now. See our guide to the [ILR changes in 2026](/ilr-changes-2026/), try our [ILR eligibility checker](/ilr-eligibility-checker/), or contact us for advice.

faqs.q: What earnings do I need for 5-year settlement?
faqs.a: £50,271 in three of the last five years under the plans announced on 2 November 2026, unless you qualify another way, such as through an eligible public service job.

faqs.q: Are the earned settlement rules in force?
faqs.a: Not yet. They’ll start to be laid from December 2026 and brought in during 2027.
Yes, for the 10-year route couples can combine earnings to reach £25,142.
People who have used public funds in the last five years would be on the 20-year route under the plans.

title: Earned Settlement Earnings Thresholds Explained
description: Earned settlement earnings thresholds for ILR: £125,141 for 3 years, £50,271 for 5 years and £12,571 for the standard 10-year route. Start dates and conditions.
